newsitem.title: USA: Woman gets dead lover's frozen sperm.
newsitem.headline: Woman gets dead lover's frozen sperm.

text.p: A woman has been given custody of 12 vials of frozen sperm left to her in a will by her lover who committed suicide more than five years ago, it was reported on Tuesday.
Deborah Hecht was willed the sperm by Bill Kane, a brilliant but emotionally troubled Los Angeles businessman, so that she could bear his children after his death, the Los Angeles Times reported.
The 12 vials of sperm, which had been stored in a cryogenics bank since Kane deposited them there in 1991, were the subject of a bitter custody battle between Hecht and Kane's grown children.

A decision by the California Supreme Court last month not to review an appeals court ruling in Hecht's favour cleared the way for the sperm to be placed in Hecht's custody and she received the vials on Monday, the Times reported.
"It's an incredible feeling," Hecht, 41, told the newspaper. I have sperm and I'm going to get preggers (pregnant) now."
Kane, an author and businessman, committed suicide in a Las Vegas hotel room in October 1991 after becoming mired in financial problems.
He left his estate to Hecht but his two children contested the will and Hecht agreed to a settlement that gave them 80 percent of their father's estate and left her with 20 percent.

That meant Hecht received 20 percent of the original 15 vials of sperm deposited by Kane. A judge ruled in 1995 that she should receive three vials, but she fought to get the other 12 after using two vials in unsuccessful attempts to get pregnant.
